chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Harun ibn Kharja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'My brother Yusuf was appointed as a custodian for these people, and in that capacity he acquired much wealth. He made that wealth into ornaments, intending to flee from the zakat. Is there zakat upon it?' He said, 'There is no zakat upon the ornaments, and whatever loss he incurred upon himself by wearing them and preventing himself from their merit is greater than what he fears from the zakat.'

key_terms.الْفَضْل: Merit/Benefit (the utility derived from the item)

ai.seo_question: Is gold jewelry worn for personal use subject to zakat in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that gold ornaments (*huliy*) worn for personal adornment are exempt from zakat, distinguishing them from stored wealth. He explains that the wearers incur a natural depreciation in value through use and derive spiritual merit by withholding the wealth from full circulation, a benefit that outweighs the zakat liability. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that utility and personal benefit can mitigate financial obligations, contrasting with the strict accumulation-focused view often applied to trade goods.
